Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1489. Arda Guler has just scored the best free-kick of the year for Turkiye

There’s something about free-kicks that makes them feel like the most Hollywood part of football.

Maybe it’s the build-up. The chance for the camera to get a close-up. The fact that players like David Beckham and Cristiano Ronaldo have made it their brand.

A perfectly executed free kick is a thing of beauty and surpassed only by a penalty in terms of unstoppable shots for a goalkeeper to face.

One of those very unstoppable shots occurred on Thursday night when Arda Guler picked out the toppest of top corners.

The Real Madrid man was representing his national team Turkiye as they faced Belgium in the Nations League and the home side took the lead through Guler in the 20th minute.

The ball is not even in an ideal spot for such a whipped free kick. It’s almost dead centre and about 10 yards away from the edge of the D. There’s a three-man wall ahead of him and a fair distance between him and the goal line.

Zadetek večera 🤩 #Arda #Guler #Turkey https://t.co/e4OE9GdE8B

— Sportklub Slovenija (@Sport_Klub_Slo) November 12, 2026

Goalkeeper Senne Lammens is hedging his bets. He stands directly in the centre of the goal, in theory making it easier for him to save a shot to his left or his right rather than gambling on one way. But it is the pace of the ball and curve that makes Senne a spectator.

Guler whips it past the head of the man on the furthest left of the wall. To be fair to Brandon Mechele, he does try and stick his head in the way of this high-flying ball and it is that kind of mentality which explains why he was wearing a protective face mask for this game.

After it flies past the Belgian centre-back’s head, it is not unfair to say the ball is about a metre high and a metre wide of the goal. If you were to pause it and ask someone which direction this ball was going, it would be a good guess to suggest row Z.

Instead, after it hits the apex of its flight plan, it curls viciously back towards the goal. If not already, Lammens is now at DEFCON 1.

The United keeper scrambles across and while his dive is pretty poor, he barely gets off the ground, he could have started on a step ladder and still not made it. The full black-gloved arm of Lammens stretches into the air but gets nowhere near it.

The ball just nips in under the crossbar. A few millimetres higher and Lammens’ blushes would have been spared. The immediate tension on the net shows just how fast the ball was moving.

It is a glorious goal and if you have seen a better free-kick all year, we will be surprised.

Turkiye’s joy was short-lived though as a quick-fire double from Belgium just seven minutes later decided the game.

Kevin De Bruyne scored the 41st goal of his international career before Atalanta’s Charles De Ketelaere put Belgium ahead.

Manchester City’s Jeremy Doku also played a starring role, assisting De Bruyne and attempting the third most dribbles in a Nations League game.

Belgium’s three points kept them in the hunt for a place in the quarter-finals and they are one point off Italy and France. Italy beat France 3-1 on the same night to consign Zinedine Zidane to his first defeat as manager.

#1486. Mauricio Pochettino is adored by his players, big on culture and good vibes, not afraid to crack the whip and does not suffer fools - exactly what dysfunctional Man United are crying out for

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER and MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 17:59 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 10 November 2026

After one press conference during Mauricio Pochettino’s ill-fated spell at Chelsea, he hosted an Argentinian-style BBQ for approximately 130 people, including his players and their families, under a marquee set up in the first-team car park at their training ground.

Returning to the room and the assembled throng of journalists still working, Pochettino popped a large plate of sausages and steaks down on the desk. He insisted it did not constitute bribery for better coverage of him. Just thought we might like to join.

This was Pochettino personified. Big on togetherness. Insisted on creating a homely environment for everyone. Believed a harmonious culture at Cobham would help performances on the pitch. Even kept a big box of lemons in his office because he reckoned they harnessed ‘energia universal’. He emphasised the importance of a good mood.

Goodness knows that’s what Manchester United need right now. And if they do decide to dismiss Michael Carrick, the prospect of managing possibly the biggest club in world football would not faze Pochettino – now the bookies’ favourite to take over.

Indeed, the 54-year-old would relish the challenge.

A few days before USA’s World Cup victory against Bosnia and Herzegovina to reach the last 16 at this summer’s tournament, coach Pochettino invited a small group of journalists to interview him at the team hotel – the Ritz-Carlton in Laguna Niguel, overlooking the Pacific Ocean 50 miles south of Los Angeles.

Manchester United could do with a dose of Mauricio Pochettino - and he would relish the challenge

The United States manager - who would cost around £7.5million to release - has openly admitted he wants to lead them in the future

Towards the end of the interview the Manchester United job came up in conversation. Pochettino turned to his long-time assistant coach Jesus Perez and said: ‘One day, your dream comes true... you go to Manchester United!’.

The Argentine clarified somewhat by explaining that Perez, while living in London, would often visit Manchester on days off to visit the National Football Museum. Perez responded with a smile: ‘United should have got you’.

One thing about Pochettino that Manchester United players will soon figure out if he takes the reins at Old Trafford is that he is not afraid to crack the whip and does not suffer fools. At the World Cup, he appeared to criticise the intervention of FIFA - and President Trump – in suspending Folarin Balogun’s ban to make the striker available for a knockout clash with Belgium.

‘I feel disappointed with too many people. They put politics and manipulation, talk about ethics and integrity [first]. If we talk about the history of this game, I am disappointed in a personal way.’

With Pochettino, you’re either all in or you’re out. Look back to his time at Tottenham for evidence of that: the decision to exile stars such as Younes Kaboul, Etienne Capoue and Paulinho into a ‘bomb squad’ - and give chances to stars such as Harry Kane - was the start of his success there.

He’s a builder of teams, works with the tools he has and makes players better. Again, that sounds like the sort of thing United are crying out for.

Pochettino is big on culture – he adopted the mantra ‘culture eats strategy for breakfast’ after a meeting with the chairman of U.S. fast food chain Chick-fil-A – and worked hard to change the holiday camp feel at the USA team. Senior stars believed they did not need to put in the extra work to keep their places. The most notable example saw national team poster-boy Christian Pulisic, once of Chelsea, attempt to skip key games after a long season for AC Milan. Pochettino put a stop to that.

The Argentine does not suffer fools, is big on culture, and can deal with big club executives - his time at Tottenham taught us that

He can manage upwards, too. He handled chairman Daniel Levy well, and credited open dialogue as being key to the partnership with the chairman which yielded a runners-up finish in the Premier League and a run to the Champions League final.

‘I speak to him a lot, we talk a lot, we have very good communication,’ Pochettino said in 2018.

‘That means sometimes we agree and sometimes we don't agree. But after, when the decision is made, we are so strong in the delivery of it which shows it is best for the club’.

His cordial relationship with Levy meant Spurs were unconcerned when he met Sir Alex Ferguson in 2016 at Scott’s in Mayfair towards the end of Louis van Gaal’s troubled reign at Old Trafford.

There was nothing untoward in that - after the restaurant meeting Pochettino returned to Spurs training, and United appointed Jose Mourinho that summer.

But he was again touted as a contender when Mourinho was dismissed two years later.

Levy sacked him in 2019, but Pochettino has remained respectful and has since praised Levy’s impact.

On the field, his time at Spurs became famous for relentless intensity - a high energy approach with a high press. Think flying full-backs Danny Rose and Kyle Walker, and all-action midfielder Mousa Dembele. For another example of him getting the best from players look at Cole Palmer. The Englishman has never since replicated his numbers from 2023-24, Pochettino’s only season at Stamford Bridge.

The football, admittedly, was a little chaotic at Chelsea. It lacked control, and not even a mountain of meat could prevent him from being quizzed about his style of play in press conferences.

Chelsea’s fans never took to Pochettino. He was the face of Spurs, after all. Pochettino might be walking his dog – a Rhodesian Ridgeback called Sansa, named after the Game of Thrones character Sansa Stark – and the odd supporter would happily stop him to have a cosy chat. But he was always going to struggle to win over the supporters in their entirety.

He once said the first time he felt a connection with Chelsea’s supporters was in April 2024 after defeating Erik Ten Hag’s United 4-3, when Cole Palmer scored twice in the 10th and 11th minutes of stoppage time. That was 11 months after he joined.

He never quite won over the fanbase of Chelsea, where his football was chaotic and his high-intensity values led to accusations that he had worsened their injury crisis

One source at the time said Pochettino wanted ‘machines’ who had the physicality to play the high-energy philosophy he craved, and like at Spurs there was indeed a great deal of high-intensity running involved in training.

However, this talk of his sessions being fitness-focused led to accusations that his methods were contributing to their crippling injury list. Pochettino disputed that, telling us he did not come ‘from Mars’ and that he knew how to manage footballers better than those on social media. He was extremely defensive whenever asked if his training was primitive.

It would be fair to debate whether United have the players to play this way – and indeed how Pochettino himself would respond to the changing landscape of the Premier League.

Spurs boss Roberto de Zerbi noted recently that upon his return to the Premier League after two years away that almost all clubs now play a more physical game than when he was at Brighton. With more teams doing the same thing that once made a Pochettino side different, how would he adapt?

We are told leaving his job in charge of the USA is more contractually feasible now than it was before the 2026 World Cup when Spurs made checks last season. He has a buyout clause, apparently worth around £7million, though that does not include the compensation required to recruit Perez and Co.

Should United require any character references, they need only ask their own Luke Shaw. He wrote the epilogue of Guillem Balague’s book Brave New World: Inside Pochettino’s Spurs, having played under him at Southampton. Shaw admitted in those pages that he would love to work with his old coach again someday. Pochettino was there for him when Shaw broke his leg – still a man-manager even when they were no longer working together.

But United could also ask any number of Chelsea players who worked with Pochettino. They largely loved him. At the time of his dismissal in May 2024, one agent of a senior figure in the changing room told us that their client was ‘devastated’. Nicolas Jackson, formerly of Chelsea and now of Aston Villa, responded to Pochettino leaving by posting two face-palm emojis on Instagram.

Pochettino had his favourites. Conor Gallagher was one of them, and the Cobham graduate's contractual situation seemed to be a source of angst between the coach and Chelsea’s hierarchy.

Players tend to love Pochettino - Luke Shaw (right), one of Manchester United's veterans, had a strong relationship with him at Southampton

His power waned at Chelsea - the club hired a set-piece coach after he insisted he didn't want one, and he was gone before the specialist arrived

As noted, Pochettino was a builder hired to work with one of the Premier League’s youngest squads but did not get the time he wanted to mould Chelsea and never hid his desire for more power at Stamford Bridge. It is said they once had the chance to sign Ansu Fati from Barcelona on favourable financial terms, but did not go through with the transfer after the manager decided he was not for him.

We did get a glimpse of Pochettino’s waning power when Daily Mail Sport asked him once whether he would like a set-piece specialist adding to his staff. He dismissed the idea, suggesting he did not need one. Chelsea then lost the Carabao Cup final when Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk headed in the winner in extra time from a corner, with Gary Neville coining the ‘blue billion-pound bottlejobs’ jibe.

A month later, Chelsea agreed a deal to hire Bernardo Cueva from Brentford to lead a new department dedicated to set-pieces. Pochettino responded by reminding us: ‘I am the head coach and I am going to decide if some people are going to be with me or not, or if I’m going to add more people or not to the touchline.’ He was gone before Cueva arrived in the summer.

An end-of-season review was held in May 2024, and Pochettino, along with Chelsea’s hierarchy, decided after a single season that it was not working. Not for him, and not for them.

Now those at the helm of United need to determine whether he is the man to bring the good vibes back, perhaps also with a little meat.

#1483. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1

Pierre Sage has his first win while Alvaro Arbeloa has lost his first three Premier League games and go to Anfield next Saturday. Frank de Boer vibes.

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

Brighton 1 Leeds 1. Pascal Gross missed a late sitter and Leeds are still winless in Brighton’s ‘new’ stadium in 11 visits.

It remains 0-0 so Spurs are goalless in three, both sides remain winless.

Iliman Ndiaye took a knock and has come off after treatment. He has sat on the bench, though, rather than headed down the tunnel, which suggests it is not an injury.

Enzo Le Fee equalises from the penalty spot.

VAR does not intervene after Lewis-Potter was penalised for holding. Le Fee chipped a pen straight at the keeper there last season.

Ellis Simms with the latest, clocking Donnarumma flush in the face with his close-range effort.

And it’s a third goal from a  left-back, but this time it’s the substitute Ben Chilwell.

Enzo jeered by Coventry fans when taken off was predictable. Replaced by Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Jaidon Anthony bundled the ball in but had used his hands.

And Mykhailo Mudryk is on for his first appearance since November 2024.

Forest are feeling aggrieved over that disallowed goal. Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot.

Big cheer for Phil Foden when he came on for Rayan Cherki. Cherki has been creative for City and this might be trying another mode of attack for Enzo Maresca or saving legs for the Champions League in midweek. They have two full days of rest before facing Porto on Tuesday.

That is a big chance for Coventry. Loum Tchaouna got room in the penalty area and it needed Gianluigi Donnarumma to save low to his right.

Luka Vuskovic heads in from an inswinging corner.

Controversy at the City Ground – and it’s again a result of Var.

Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Neco Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goalline.

The goal did go to Var for a possible handball by Williams, and it was ruled that the Wales international did handle it. Did look very harsh.

Coventry are still in this game but City have their chances to put them away. Enzo was deemed offside when he set up a strike for Haaland. The UK’s most expensive player has got better during this game.

Looks like it will be ruled out for handball.

Vitaly Janelt breaks the deadlock after Brentford were battered in the first half.

Keith Andrews is a brave manager. Having been forced into a change after 17 minutes when his captain, Nathan Collisn was injured, he shook it up at half-time by replacing three of his biggest signings, Kayode, Sangaré and Ouattara for Hickey, Yarmoliuk and Anthony.

There might be a VAR check but Neco Williams is in like Flynn when Tonali makes a bad mistake.

Mohammed Kudus comes on for Sávio and Andy Robertson for Destiny Udogie.

Igor Jesus and Daniel Muñoz come on for Ola Aina and Dan Ndoye.

Tyrick Mitchell has scored his second. What do they say about London buses…

Mitchell rampaging up the left, shoots. It’s blocked by García who tries to clear by hitting it straight into Mitchell’s foot whence it ricochets past Bernd Leno.

It was the culmination of a long passage of huffing and puffing after Marmoush had scudded a free-kick straight into the Forest wall.

Forest are clinging on a bit at the moment with some pretty desperate defending.

It was put in by Jacob Strand Larsen, who came on for Eddie Nketiah at half-time but he was offside.

With Tottenham appearing so toothless in attack, you have to wonder whether Roberto De Zerbi ends the long wait for Mykhailo Mudryk.

It is over 600 days since Mudryk last played a competitive match.

There is also the option of Dominic Solanke on the bench too.

Tanaka was offside when he turned in Stach’s free-kick. Leeds squander opportunity to double their lead.

Because of the 4½ minute VAR check for the Ballard ‘goal’ and an injury to Nathan Collins that forced the Bees’ captain off.

These are clearly two teams in transition.

Tottenham have spent over £300m this summer and are still waiting for lift-off.

Forest are embarking on a new era under Oliver Glasner with a style of play that will take time to implement.

It’s been a messy game so far with both teams struggling to impose themselves.

The best chance fell to one of Tottenham’s new arrivals, Omar Marmoush, but he drilled a shot wide of the post.

Josh King scores one and makes one. César Palacios with the rebound after Gonzalo García’s effort was parried to him.

Oliver Glasner’s wife Bettina is making her first visit to the City Ground today.

Glasner said that he is hoping to celebrate dinner tonight with his first three points since taking charge.

In a ding-dong match, the left-back, Tyrick Mitchell, pounces to fire Palace level.

Lewis Dunk saves Brighton after Calvert-Lewin had rounded Verbruggen and tried to slide it in on the angle.

Erling Haaland at the back post with a thunderous header – his 300th goal in club football.

Kamada was offside by a gnat’s whisker. VAR is making this job ridiculous.

Both Calvert-Lewin and Tanaka should have finished but Bogle was there to make sure. Elvedi spun on to the ball in the right of the penalty area to stand up a left-foot cross to the back post. Calvert-Lewin leapt and powered a low header hat Rushworth scooped out. Tanaka, following up, sliced his shot from five yards across goal where Bogle blindsided a defender to tap it in.

Kamada equalises at the Cottage, played in by an excellent pass from Pino.

Coventry fans are in good voice – and jeering Enzo Fernandez when he gets the ball. The Argentina midfielder has been quiet so far.

Messy start here at the City Ground with both teams struggling for fluency.

Tottenham are still waiting for their first goal of the season with a drastically reshaped team.

Danso was deemed to be interfering with play in an offside position, blocking the goalkeeper’s view of Ballard’s strike.

Disasi gives the ball away to Charles who finds Bobb. His pass sets up King for a shot which is deflected past Henderson.

Kevin Danso was standing in front of Kelleher in an offside position.

Was a Sunderland player blocking the goalkeeper?

Dan Ballard opens the scoring at the GTech from a free-kick.

Cherki makes headway down the left and sends over a dipping, menacing cross towards Enzo who is pushed high as a No10 but Carl Rushworth plucks it out of the air.

It’s Enzo Fernández replacing Nico O’Reilly not Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Enzo Fernandez will start, it has been confirmed, with O’Reilly injured in the warm-up

Fernandez is lined up in the tunnel ready to come out.

England left-back, who was slated to play in midfield, hurt his back/hip in the warm-up.

Seems to have a problem with his lower back or hip. He has been ruled out of the match.

One pleasing thing about the signing of Melvin Bard by Leeds is the prospect of it reviving oft-heard Elland Road shouts from 1989-92 of ‘Giyit Mel’ and ‘G’won Mel’ in encouragement of the sainted Sterland, the Zico of Fullerton Park.

You can follow all the reaction and a report from Newcastle’s 2-2 draw with Bournemouth here.

Liam Delap will make his first start for Forest today after becoming the club’s record signing this summer.

It was a relatively quiet transfer window for the club, which has not always been the case since their return to the Premier League in 2022.

The big headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

#1482. Lookman keen on leaving Atletico, Roma at the window

Roma is looking for a dynamic winger who can bring pace and power to the Giallorossi’s attack.

Gian Piero Gasperini has plenty of quality up front with Dybala, Soulé, Mora, and Pellegrini, but lacks physical strength; he doesn’t have a Gervinho-like player.

This is why the club is monitoring the future of Ademola Lookman, currently playing for Atletico Madrid.

Lookman’s potential transfer to the capital would allow the Roma manager to reunite with one of the key players from his time at Atalanta.

Under the guidance of the general from Grugliasco, the Nigerian striker achieved particularly high levels of performance, establishing himself as one of the most effective wingers in Europe.

Ademola Lookman has played 735 minutes of football this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist for Atlético Madrid. His performances are significantly different from those he had in Bergamo under Gasperini.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the 1997-born player is dissatisfied with his experience with the Colchoneros, which is why his agent has announced he would like to leave Simeone’s side. This is a situation Roma is closely monitoring, although it remains a difficult move to finalize in January.

#1481. Man Utd’s 2027-28 Championship predicted XI if they’re relegated this season

Manchester United find themselves in the bottom three after their worst-ever start to a Premier League season, and relegation is now a distinct possibility.

United are set to replace Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino in a bid to turn their form around, but there’s no guarantee that it will work.

If United are relegated, most of their big-name players would look to leave, and they would have to reduce the wage bill. We’ve made a predicted Championship XI for United, arranged in a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Despite enduring a poor start to the 2026-27 season, Senne Lammens is still one of the best young goalkeepers in Europe and will not be short on suitors if United are relegated.

Darlow joined United in the summer and is currently the back-up goalkeeper at Old Trafford, but relegation from the Premier League could see him get a promotion on an individual level.

He has made 161 appearances in the second tier and is a two-time Championship winner, lifting the title with Newcastle in 2017 and Leeds in 2025.

Diogo Dalot is the second-longest serving player in the United squad, but has become a much-maligned figure at Old Trafford and is unlikely to stick around for a year in the Championship.

Pochettino’s impending arrival at United could lead to a move for Trippier, who made 114 appearances under the manager during his time at Tottenham.

He is currently playing for Wolves in the Championship and they are targeting an immediate return to the Premier League, but the boyhood United fan would surely jump at the chance to move to Old Trafford.

Maguire celebrates his 34th birthday next year and is widely expected to leave Old Trafford when his contract expires at the end of the season.

But if United are relegated, they could offer him a new deal on reduced terms as his experience and leadership qualities would make him a real asset in the Championship.

The centre-back has made 43 appearances in the second tier and was part of the Hull City side that won promotion via the play-offs in 2015-16.

Heaven joined United from Arsenal in a £1million deal in January 2025 and is one of the lowest-paid players in the squad, taking home a £35,000-per-week salary.

The 20-year-old centre-back initially showed a lot of promise at Old Trafford, but has struggled for form in the opening weeks of this season.

While he would likely be offered the chance to make an immediate return to the Premier League, a season in the Championship and the promise of regular starts could be good for his development.

United retain an interest in Lewis Hall following their tentative enquiries for the Newcastle left-back last summer, but relegation would bring an end to that pursuit.

Harry Amass made 22 appearances in the Championship last season and could finally get a chance in the United team if they drop down to the second tier, but a move for Mitchell feels more likely.

The 27-year-old has entered the final year of his Crystal Palace contract and will be available on a free transfer next summer.

United spent £155million on a midfield overhaul, but relegation to the Championship could see Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans all depart after just one season.

In this scenario, they should pursue a move for Hackney, who won the EFL Championship Player of the Season and the PFA Championship Players’ Player of the Year awards in the 2025/26 campaign.

He left Middlesbrough and completed a £16.5million move to Everton last summer but finds himself behind James Garner and Harrison Armstrong in the pecking order, making just one Premier League start this season.

Dropping back down to the Championship may feel like a backwards step, but playing for United every week is still an appealing prospect.

Kobbie Mainoo has been on United’s books since the age of nine and recently put pen to paper on a contract that ties him to his boyhood club until 2031.

But the midfielder was willing to leave United last year after falling out of the England squad, and a year in the Championship would be detrimental to his chances of playing at Euro 2028.

His departure would hand more opportunities to fellow United academy graduate Tyler Fletcher, who made two first-team appearances last season and won the Denzil Haroun Reserve Team Player of the Year award.

The 19-year-old is also a senior Scotland international and, unlike Mainoo, playing every week in the Championship would help him get selected for Euro 2028.

Lacey has long been heralded as one of the most exciting talents in United’s academy, and he was linked with a loan move to the Championship last summer.

The 19-year-old stayed at Old Trafford and scored in the Carabao Cup against Brighton before coming off the bench to set up the winning goal against Roma in the Champions League.

But he’s yet to start a Premier League game and could be playing every week in the Championship next season, albeit while still remaining at United.

Bruno Fernandes has shown a lot of loyalty towards United during a turbulent period for the club and rejected a £700,000-per-week offer from the Saudi Pro League following their 15th-placed finish in 2024-25.

But relegation to the Championship would be a step too far for the Portugal international, who would have a line of clubs queuing up to secure his signature.

Mount has predominantly been a back-up to Fernandes throughout his time at United, while also struggling with a number of injury issues.

The midfielder was part of the Derby County side that reached the play-off final in 2018-19, and could get his career back on track by playing regular football in the Championship for a season.

He may have to take a pay cut though, with his current wage reported to be around £150,000-per-week.

Despite admitting that he prefers to play at left-back, Dorgu has become increasingly influential in the final third.

The Denmark international registered eight direct goal contributions in 13 appearances under Carrick, including a goal and an assist in his final game.

His pace, physicality and brilliant ball-striking ability would make him the Gareth Bale of the Championship.

United may not be in the relegation zone if Benjamin Sesko had been fully fit this season, but the £74million signing is too good to be playing in the Championship.

Moves for the likes of Jean-Philippe Mateta, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Serhou Guirassy would also be unrealistic, so United may have to shop in the Championship.

Lankshear is currently the best striker in the second tier, having netted 13 goals in 13 league appearances for Middlesbrough this season.

The 21-year-old is seen as a long-term successor to Harry Kane in the England side, and firing United back to the Premier League would be great for his burgeoning reputation.

#1478. Roma concede 4 times more without Kone on the pitch

In their final match before the international break, Roma won 3-0 against Sassuolo, benefiting once again from the presence of Manu Koné, who had been sidelined during the first half against Real Madrid.

The French midfielder immediately delivered a performance of substance and quality: interceptions, free-throws, and a pace-setting performance with the ball at his feet.

The balance that the 2001-born player brings to the team is crucial, so much so that upon his return to the pitch, the Giallorossi team remained clean. A coincidence?

With Koné on the pitch, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport, Roma have conceded only four goals in eight games (0.5), not including the 17 minutes against Real Madrid. Without the French midfielder, however, the average quadruples: 14 goals (2) conceded in seven matches (including the 3-4 loss to Real Madrid).

This data isn’t solely attributable to the absence of the 2001-born player, but there’s a clear sense that with him, Roma are more balanced and protected.

After the break, Gian Piero Gasperini will be able to rely on his cornerstone again.

While waiting to see what his future holds, Koné will enter the fourth year of his contract at the end of the year, so there are two options: a renewal with a pay rise or a painful transfer. The French midfielder’s dream remains PSG, Roma’s next opponent in the Champions League.

#1477. Can you name Mauricio Pochettino’s 25 most-used players in his career?

Mauricio Pochettino is regarded as one of the best managers of his generation, but can you name the 25 players he’s used the most across his career on the sidelines?

Having played with distinction as a rugged defender in the 1990s and 2000s, Pochettino’s first job as a manager came at Espanyol.

After three years at the Barcelona-based club, the Argentine got his first Premier League job when Southampton appointed him in January 2013. His free-flowing football and willingness to blood young players caught the attention of bigger clubs.

#1476. Four ideal signings for Mauricio Pochettino’s Man Utd in January

Mauricio Pochettino is set to take the reins at Manchester United and they’ll be hoping for an immediate boost in their fortunes – but they might have to add to their squad at the next opportunity to give themselves the best chance.

United’s season so far has been a disaster. They’ve gone into the international break sitting in the Premier League’s relegation zone. It’s cost Michael Carrick his job as manager, but quite rightly, the blame is more widespread.

United’s owners, directors and players have all come in for criticism, but if anything’s going to change, it’s probably the latter.

It’d be wrong to expect a mass overhaul in January, a notoriously difficult transfer window to do big business in, but it’d be equally daft to expect United to just sit around and do nothing.

A new manager coming in gives them a chance to bring in new ideas and players to suit those ideas.

So, keeping it semi-realistic, who’d be a good signing for them under Pochettino?

It’s tempting whenever a manager gets a new job to look at who’s at his former clubs that he might like to reunite with.

Ironically in this case, the one familiar player that might most appeal from Tottenham isn’t someone Pochettino worked with at Tottenham – it’s been a while, after all – but at Chelsea instead.

Gallagher was Pochettino’s most-used player during his sole season at Chelsea, playing in 48 of his 51 games in charge.

Sure, United already did a lot of work on their midfield over the summer, but they still seem to be missing runners there. And if there’s one thing Gallagher can do, it’s run. And if there’s one thing Pochettino wants his midfielders to do… you get the picture.

On average, Gallagher has covered 12.2km per 90 minutes when playing in the Premier League this season. It’s the highest average in the squad of anyone with three or more starts.

Pochettino used to rave about Gallagher at Chelsea. Exhibit A, this ringing endorsement in February 2024:

“He is a player with a great commitment to the team. He is always trying to compensate in every situation, in offensive and defensive situations. It’s priceless to have a player like him.

“‘He is in the starting XI nearly every game and one of the captains. For me, he is the type of player that the club need to have.

“He runs, he plays, he fights. He does everything to win. He is a really important player that the coaching staff want to have on the team.”

Gallagher hasn’t exactly been a regular starter for Spurs this season, but he only joined them in January, so he might be tricky to prise away.

But hypothetically, he’d get more of a look in from Pochettino in a midfield where Kobbie Mainoo is a top prospect, but Carlos Baleba has had injury issues, Youri Tielemans hasn’t convinced with his energy and Andrey Santos remains an unknown quantity.

Santos spent the 2023-24 season out on loan away from Chelsea rather than as part of Pochettino’s squad.

Gallagher would add to United’s homegrown quota too, but for a Pochettino team, he wouldn’t just be making up the numbers.

Pochettino got the best out of Luke Shaw when they worked together at Southampton, but Luke Shaw then was different to Luke Shaw now.

Back in those days he was a talented teenage prospect. Nowadays, he’s United’s tired only natural option at left-back. Quite simply, they need to freshen it up.

Pochettino will probably be happy to keep Shaw around as a senior, trustworthy figure. But he’ll be wanting more energy from the full-back positions and that means fresh legs.

Some of Pochettino’s best teams thrived when their full-backs bombed on to offer width while the wingers cut inside. Shaw can’t really do that anymore.

One player who can get up and down the flank is Palace’s Mitchell, who might not be the most inspiring choice but could be the best of what’s available.

Palace’s precarious position, coupled with the fact that Mitchell is out of contract at the end of the season, could make January his ideal time to escape.

His attacking output hasn’t always been cited as a strong point, but he can cover plenty of ground up and down the channel. A Pochettino team don’t necessarily need their full-backs to be the ones getting goals and assists, just to offer support and threatening runs.

Mitchell also has a good record in duels and could offer United more stability in defence, as they desperately need. There might be a signing with a higher ceiling to make, but that’s the kind of thing that might have to wait until the summer.

It’s not just at left-back United need to upgrade. The battle between Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui on the other side is hardly awe-inspiring, but unless they can shift one or the other, finding an upgrade might be a summer job.

At centre-back, though, they might not be able to afford to wait. Getting Harry Maguire back from injury will be a boost when the time comes, but with Lisandro Martinez suffering a sharp downturn in form, a brand new centre-back would help.

We reckon Nottingham Forest’s Murillo would be a pretty smart signing for United. He’s strong and imposing but also good on the ball, which is perfect for Pochettino.

Is he gettable in January, though? Probably not. He signed a new contract in the summer and we know what Forest are like when it comes to selling players. Or stopping them from being sold.

File this one under the dream signing category. Murillo has Premier League experience, plenty of good years still ahead of him and the attributes that Pochettino values highly in his defenders.

Look, we can safely say Pochettino would love to work with Harry Kane again. We know there have been numerous times when United would have loved to sign Harry Kane. It’s just not happening, though, is it?

Ink dry on his new Bayern Munich contract, Kane is off the menu. But a striker is still high on United’s wish list.

By January, Benjamin Sesko will be just about ready to return from injury, but who knows in what state. In his absence, United don’t have great alternatives. Joshua Zirkzee has had enough chances now and not taken them, while Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are probably better out wide.

The summer transfer window is usually the more likely option for big striker moves. United could still do with someone to put them on, though.

The right kind of middle-ground between luxury signing and mere stop-gap could be someone like Borussia Dortmund’s Guirassy.

He’s the same height as Kane at 6’2 and boasts some similar strengths, such as his link-up play and chance conversion.

With eight goals from 14 games this season, including four from four in the Champions League, he’s in solid form. It’s no anomaly, looking at his last few seasons: 22 goals last time out, 38 the season before, 30 in the one before that.

At 30 years old, he’s not necessarily the long-term solution. But Kane is 33 and you’d sign him, wouldn’t you?

Guirassy might be one of the best options out there in terms of value for money.

#1474. The 10 players Chelsea let go in the summer – & how they’re faring elsewhere

Chelsea have become known for their revolving door transfer policy, but only 10 first-teamers left Stamford Bridge this summer. Amateurs.

Xabi Alonso pivoted to a more football-first policy, signing veterans like Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, alongside a proper goalkeeper in Emi Martinez.

Several of the squad that staggered to 10th in 2025-26 left the club, with Chelsea raking in over £500million for them. We’ve seen how they’ve fared since.

Chelsea were reluctant to sell Cucurella, but Real Madrid swooped in during the World Cup and paid £47.5million for the defender.

He’s already nailed down the left-back spot under Jose Mourinho, ahead of Alvaro Carreras and Ferland Mendy.

The 28-year-old has made 15 appearances for Madrid in all competitions and did a superb job shutting down Lamine Yamal in El Clasico last month. Chelsea are yet to properly replace him.

Another player that Chelsea fans were sad to see leave, George joined Everton in an £18million deal. The winger spent the second half of last season on loan there and David Moyes wanted him back.

He’s been getting plenty of minutes given the ultra-slim size of Everton’s squad, with eight appearances and a goal against Manchester United in September.

Santos moved to Manchester United in July for an initial fee of £48million. This was a player linked with Graham Potter’s West Ham 12 months previously and did little to improve his reputation since.

Still, United thought they’d got a bargain. Until they saw Santos play and realised Chelsea were laughing all the way to the bank.

The main memory of Santos’ early United career has been lying on his back as Morgan Rogers ran in a straight line past him to score on Halloween.

Perhaps Mauricio Pochettino can find better use for him.

Chalobah was a solid Premier League defender, but probably not quite good enough for where Chelsea want to be.

Given he’d also qualify as pure profit under financial regulations, it was no surprise to see the Blues cash in and sell him to Como for £25.7million.

Cesc Fabregas has played Chalobah eight times – six in Serie A and twice in the Champions League – and he also played in England’s Nations League victory in Prague in October.

After an inauspicious year at Stamford Bridge, there were plenty of eyebrows raised when Nottingham Forest paid £45million for Delap.

It looked like money not well spent after Forest’s goal-shy start to the season, but Delap really announced himself with two goals against Manchester City.

They were both thunderous strikes. Talk of an England call-up was premature, but here is another player who has probably found his level.

Jackson has blossomed since joining Aston Villa for an initial £47.5million, reaping the benefits of working under Unai Emery again after their previous stint at Villarreal.

The Senegal striker has scored nine times in 14 Villa appearances, including a match-winning double against Manchester City in October.

This was a player who always had evident talent, but without the time and faith to fully show it at Chelsea. It’s hard not to feel pleased for him.

After joining in January 2023, Fofana failed to give a succession of Chelsea managers much of a reason to play him.

The striker had loan spells at Union Berlin, Burnley, Goztepe, Fatih Karagumruk and Strasbourg while slipping out of supporters’ consciousness.

He left the club this summer for a measly £2.3million, a rare loss on the balance sheet for BlueCo. He’s scored once in five appearances for Swiss side Servette.

Tosin was only 28 when he left Chelsea, but their squad was so young that he was affectionately known as ‘Unc’ by his team-mates.

Like Chalobah, Tosin was a decent Premier League defender without the ceiling required. Spurs paid £10million for him and he’s played just twice since his move due to injury.

The biggest transfer saga of the summer was dragged out until Deadline Day, where Chelsea eventually got their £125million asking price.

Enzo Maresca desperately wanted Fernandez at Manchester City, but it’s not gone swimmingly since.

The Argentina midfielder has become a scapegoat in City’s run of three league defeats, apparently holding back Elliot Anderson with his lack of athleticism.

According to FotMob, Fernandez has won just 44.9 per cent of his total duels this season. Not ideal for half of a central midfield pairing.

Figuring out how to fit Fernandez into City’s XI is one of Maresca’s most pressing tasks. Chelsea will be pleased not to have that problem anymore.

Guiu also bid farewell to Stamford Bridge on deadline day, joining RB Leipzig on a permanent deal worth up to £14.6million with add-ons.

The striker wasn’t a first-team regular but still scored eight goals in 29 matches across all competitions. Not bad, given this included six goals in their Conference League-winning campaign in 2024-25.

The 20-year-old is yet to find the net for his new club.

#1473. Sarina Wiegman receives honorary damehood from Prince William at Windsor Castle - after leading Lionesses to back-to-back European titles

Published: 14:28 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 10 November 2026

Lionesses manager Sarina Wiegman has been awarded an honorary damehood by Prince William after leading England to back-to-back Euro wins.

Wiegman is Dutch and therefore cannot be made a substantive dame. Instead she has picked up the honorary title, because the Netherlands does not have a British monarch as its head of state.

She said upon being awarded the title at Windsor Castle on Tuesday: 'I feel very privileged to receive my honorary Damehood from His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales at Windsor Castle today.

'It is a day I will never forget and made even more special by sharing it with members of my family.

'I would like to again express my sincere gratitude for this honour and for the continued respect and warmth I experience from the English people. I thank everyone for their support.'

Wiegman was named in the King's New Year's Honours list at the end of 2025, alongside several members of her England team.

England manager Sarina Wiegman (left) has been awarded an honourary damehood by Prince William (right)

Captain Leah Williamson was awarded a CBE, with Alex Greenwood, Keira Walsh, Georgia Stanway and Ella Toone all being honoured with MBEs.

Wiegman said at the time: 'I would like to express my sincere gratitude for this honour. When I first arrived in England, I could never have imagined the respect and warmth I've experienced from the English people. I deeply thank the fans for their support.

'This title is a reflection of my exceptional team of players and staff. My congratulations go to Alex, Ella, Georgia, Keira, Leah and also Dr Ritan Mehta who have all been celebrated for their brilliant contributions.

'Our team values mean that when there is recognition for one, then there is recognition for all. I want to pay tribute to every member of our EURO squad. They should all be celebrated for everything they brought to the pitch and for the positive role they play in society. I'm proud to work alongside such a dedicated group of people.'

The former Netherlands coach took over the England team in 2021 and led them to success at Euro 2022 and Euro 2025.

She also reached the World Cup final in 2023, and signed a new two-year contract extension earlier this year, which will take her to the end of the 2029 Euros.

#1471. Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”

Possession: Arsenal 55%-45% ChelseaShots: 16-13Shots on target: 9-5Corners: 5-3Touches in opposition box: 44-25

The final whistle is blown at the Emirates and Arsenal maintain their 100% record through three games as they have beaten Chelsea 2-1. They were 1-0 down inside the opening two minutes but goals from Havertz and Odegaard have led them to victory. Chelsea suffer their first competitive defeat under Xabi Alonso.

Pedro’s cross from the right has too much on it and Chavarria cannot head it back across goal. Chelsea’s last chance might have been that Estevao effort which was brilliantly saved by Raya.

That is a stunning save from Raya that may have preserved Arsenal’s victory. Estevao cuts in from the right and curls one towards the top corner. It looks set for the net but somehow Raya makes a fantastic save to deny Estevao.

Chelsea are bringing on Welbeck for Rogers, who is jeered by the Arsenal fans. Welbeck comes on with a note, that he gives to his captain James.

Arsenal have lost a bit of their composure and structure. I suspect that’s why Arteta has turned to Mikel Merino. He screamed at his bench immediately after a messy passage of play, and Merino emerged about 20 seconds later. Merino is very much the “sensible adult” sort of player, who should calm things down. Although he hasn’t yet.

England team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a big club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...

It has kicked off. Rogers is cynically tripped by Rice but the referee somehow does not see it. Rogers is incensed and marches over to Rice, who has massively got away with one there. Rice knew exactly what he was doing as he deliberately trips Rogers. That is a nasty from Rice, who avoids a booking, yet Rogers is shown a yellow card. That is frankly dreadful refereeing.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

Estevao is brought on for Chelsea in place of Neto.

Pedro wins a corner off Gabriel out on the left in front of the travelling Chelsea fans. Gusto’s delivery to the back post is caught at the second attempt by Raya.

Double change for Arsenal as Gyokeres and Merino come on for Havertz and Odegaard.

Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. He plays the ball inside towards Havertz, who is in space on the edge of the Chelsea box. It is really intelligent from Havertz, who dummies it to take away Fofana and allows the ball to run through to Odegaard, who takes one touch before firing past Martinez.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Arsenal just scored the same goal they scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield. Tzolis into Odegaard, low and fast.

As it stands, Manchester City will be the only team with a 100% record after three games.

I think Chelsea are now 19 Premier League games without keeping a clean sheet, dating back to last season.

A few Chelsea players were having a moan at referee Christopher Kavanagh as they went off for half-time. But Alonso’s players need to calm down and keep their cool. There were signs the Blues’ old disciplinary problems could rear their head again with Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer being booked. Romeo Lavia also squared up to Ben White for no real reason. Chelsea have to keep 11 players on the pitch.
